column1: # *** IS THERE A JUAN CARLOS LERENA IN ITALIAN RECORDS? - asked and tested 16 September 2026. ***
# David's question, and it is a better one than it looks, because the archive's own DNA page already
# argues that *** Pablo Armando had about one Italian parent *** and that the signal is NORTHERN.
# *** METHOD: EXACT MATCH, because the default is not. *** A fuzzy FamilySearch search for LERENA in
# Italy returns *** 9,112 *** and is worthless - the results include Lorino, Loreno, Lorena, Lorosano
# and Lorrai. *** Forcing exact match returns 66. *** Every number below is exact-match.
query
*** LERENA, exact, Italy ***
column3: *** THE SURNAME IS ITALIAN AS WELL AS SPANISH, AND THIS ARCHIVE DID NOT KNOW THAT. *** The cluster is the *** DIOCESE OF TORINO *** - Bartolomeo, Teresa, Anna Maria, Eduardo, Caterina, Luigi, Paolo, Giovanni, Giuseppe, Vincenzo, Giacomo, Margherita, Domenica, Maddalena, Adelaide, Irma. *** All Italian forenames, in Piedmont. ***

column1: *** LERENA + forename CARLO, exact, Italy ***
column3: *** A CONTROLLED NULL: *** the identical search without a forename returns 66, so the mechanism works and the surname is in the index. *** There is no Carlo Lerena in Italy at all. ***

column1: *** LERINA, exact, Italy ***
column3: Also Torino-centred, plus *** Ivrea, Catania, Messina and Mantova. *** *** This is the commoner Italian spelling of the two ***, which matters because CEMLA has Lerinas landing at Buenos Aires.

column1: *** LERINA + forename CARLO ***
column3: Carlo Lerina b. 18 Dec 1917 Torino (too late); *** CARLO DOMENICO LERINA, baptised IVREA 30 May 1858, born 28 May 1858, parents ANTONIO LERINA and GIUSEPPA PEAN-CONTO *** ; one at Catania 1846; two without dates. *** Only the Ivrea man is age-plausible - he would be 23 when Pablo Armando was born. NOTHING WHATEVER TIES HIM TO ARGENTINA, and he is recorded here as a name-shaped coincidence, not a candidate. ***

column1: *** LERINA + forename GIOVANNI ***
column2: *** 6 records, NONE of them Giovanni Carlo. ***
column3: The best-dated is *** Giovanni Lerina, b. 1863, marriage banns at Torino 24 April 1887, parents Luigi and Luigia Cosi *** - *** which rules him out twice over: *** he was 19 when Pablo Armando was born, and he was posting banns in Turin five years later, so he was in Italy.

column1: # *** THE ANSWER TO THE QUESTION AS ASKED: NO. ***
# *** There is no GIOVANNI CARLO or GIAN CARLO Lerena or Lerina anywhere in FamilySearch's Italian
# index, under either spelling. *** Carlo and Giovanni both occur; they never occur together.
# *** BUT THE SEARCH TURNED UP SOMETHING BETTER THAN A NAME, AND IT CONVERGES WITH THE DNA. ***
# The archive's DNA page already reasons: Cheryl is *** 11.1% Italian at MyHeritage ***, her other three
# grandparents are not Italian, *** which implies roughly 44% in Pablo Armando - about one Italian
# parent *** - and the split is *** NORTHERN-DOMINANT, 6.1% north against 3.6% south. ***
# *** The Italian Lerenas and Lerinas are in TURIN and IVREA. That is Piedmont. That is the north. ***
# *** Two independent things now point the same way *** - an admixture estimate and a surname
# distribution - *** and neither of them is a record naming anybody. Stated as convergence, not proof. ***
# *** WHY THIS NULL IS WEAKER THAN THE COUNT MAKES IT LOOK. ***
# *** FamilySearch's Italian coverage is partial and wildly uneven by province. *** Civil registration
# is indexed for some tribunali and not others; church records for some dioceses and not others.
# *** A man who left for Argentina before 1882 may have no indexed Italian record at all *** - and if he
# was baptised GIOVANNI and became JUAN CARLOS on the far side of the Atlantic, *** the Carlos may never
# have existed in Italy to be indexed. *** That is the ordinary shape of an emigrant's name.
# *** So: no Juan Carlos found, and the absence proves very little. ***
# =================== AND THEN ANTENATI, WHICH DAVID ASKED FOR NEXT ===================
# *** THE PORTALE ANTENATI - antenati.cultura.gov.it - IS THE ITALIAN STATE ARCHIVES' OWN CIVIL
# REGISTRATION PORTAL, and it was the right thing to ask for ***, because the caveat on the FamilySearch
# work above was precisely that FamilySearch's Italian coverage is uneven. Antenati is the source itself.
query
*** LERENA, whole national name index ***
column2: *** ONE record. *** *** CESARE LERENA, atto di morte 1915, Stato civile italiano > BRESCIA > Morti > 1915 ***, Archivio di Stato di Brescia. Spouse *** Rosa Barbaleni. ***
column3: *** Not our man, and not Piedmont - Brescia is Lombardy. *** Still northern Italy, which is the only thing about it worth noting.

column1: *** LERINA, whole national name index ***
column2: *** 8 records ***, and *** most of them are "DI LERINA", which is a different surname. *** The plain Lerinas are Ellene, Giovanna and Elizabetta.
column3: *** No Carlo. No Giovanni. No Giovanni Carlo. ***

column1: # *** BUT DO NOT RECORD THAT AS A NULL, BECAUSE THE CONTROL DESTROYS IT. ***
# *** Antenati HOLDS 2,621 REGISTERS FOR TORINO. *** The images are there. The question is whether the
# NAME INDEX - which is what a surname search actually searches - reaches them.
control
*** Search the name index for ROSSI, restricted to Torino *** - a surname that cannot be absent
column2: *** 102 results *** - and the forenames are *** CHARLES, MARGUERITE, JACINTE. French. *** Years present: *** 1805, 1808, 1809, 1810, 1811. ***
column3: *** THE TORINO NAME INDEX IS NAPOLEONIC ONLY. *** Piedmont was annexed to France, civil registration was kept in French, and *** that is the window Antenati has indexed: about 1805 to 1811. *** *** It does not reach the 1840s to the 1880s, which is the whole of the period that matters for a man who fathered a child in 1882. ***

column1: # *** SO THE ANSWER ON ANTENATI IS: NOTHING, AND THE NOTHING MEANS NOTHING. ***
# *** For Piedmont in the relevant period Antenati's images exist and are NOT NAME-SEARCHABLE. *** A
# surname search there was never capable of finding him. *** This is the same lesson as the Rosario
# typescript index and the FreeREG Devon parishes: the null belongs to the finding aid, not to the past. ***
# *** WHAT IS ACTUALLY SEARCHABLE FOR THE RIGHT YEARS, AND IT IS NOT ANTENATI. ***
# *** FamilySearch's "Italy, Torino, Torino, Civil Registration (Tribunale), 1866-1899" IS indexed ***
# and is where the 66 Lerena and 114 Lerina above came from. *** That is the collection to work ***, by
# parent name, for a Lerina or Lerena male born about 1840-1862 who then leaves the Italian record.
# *** Antenati's 2,621 Torino registers remain the fallback ***: browsable by comune and year, image by
# image, the way this archive read Rosario and Canelones. *** Expensive, and possible. ***
# ============ AND THEN THE SAME SPELLING BACK IN ARGENTINA, 16 September 2026 ============
# *** The archive has worked LERENA hard in Argentina and has never swept LERINA, which is the
# commoner ITALIAN spelling. *** Done now, exact match.
query
*** LERINA, exact, Argentina ***
column2: *** 26 records. *** La Rioja and Santiago del Estero church records, the 1895 national census, cemetery records, military records.
column3: *** Thinly scattered and mostly nowhere near Santa Fe. *** No family group, no cluster, nothing resembling a household at Rosario.

column1: *** The one that is worth writing down ***
column2: *** JUAN LERINA, age 64, estimated birth 1862, BURIED 4 APRIL 1926 at SANTA FE, LA CAPITAL, SANTA FE, ARGENTINA. *** FamilySearch ark 1:1:6575-KRRP, Argentina Cemetery Records. *** Image Unavailable. ***
column3: *** RECORDED AS A COINCIDENCE, NOT A CANDIDATE, and the reasons are worth stating so nobody promotes it later. *** *** FOR: *** the surname is the Italian spelling, he is in *** SANTA FE PROVINCE ***, and a birth about 1862 is not impossible for a man whose son was born in February 1882. *** AGAINST, and it is heavier: *** he is *** JUAN, not JUAN CARLOS ***; he is at *** SANTA FE LA CAPITAL, which is 170 km north of ROSARIO *** and a different city entirely; a birth in 1862 makes him *** twenty *** when Pablo Armando was born; and *** the image is unavailable, so the burial entry itself cannot be read. *** *** Four loose fits and no join. This archive has been wrong before by promoting exactly this shape of thing. ***

column1: # *** AND IT DOES NOT TOUCH THE ARCHIVE'S STANDING CLAIM, WHICH IS STILL TRUE AS WRITTEN. ***
# The front page says *** "No Juan Carlos Lerena appears in any indexed record in Argentina or Uruguay." ***
# *** That remains literally true: this man is Juan LERINA, not Juan Carlos LERENA. *** The sentence was
# checked against this find rather than left to rot, which is the only reason to write a find like this down.
# *** CEMLA COULD NOT BE RUN, AND THE REASON IS A HARD STOP. ***
# The plan was to re-run CEMLA for both spellings *** before 1882 ***, since the earliest arrival the
# archive holds under any spelling is the Lerina family of *** 15 March 1889 ***. The search moved to
# *** search.cemla.com and it is behind a CAPTCHA *** - the form carries CaptchaCode and
# LBD_VCID_SampleCaptcha fields. *** This session does not complete CAPTCHAs. It is David's to run. ***
# *** AND THERE IS A PRIOR QUESTION HE SHOULD SETTLE FIRST, because it may make the search pointless: ***
# *** CEMLA's arrivals database is generally given as beginning in 1882. *** If that is right, then an
# arrival before February 1882 is *** invisible to it by construction ***, and the absence of one proves
# nothing at all. *** Check the stated coverage before spending the searches. ***
